doctor: Protect players who can gather information across several nights.
Keep your role private when possible; the Horror has reason to target you.
detective: Cross-check every result: one Villager is a false positive, and fear or drunkenness can distort your information.
Share findings carefully so you can keep investigating.
watchman: Watch players the Horror may target or players whose visitors you want to verify.
A hidden Wraith may escape notice, so compare your results with other claims.
bodyguard: Find an ally whose survival matters. If the Storyteller confirms they will die at night, you can take their place.
psychic: Ask each player you visit what role type they claim, then look for a pattern across nights.
A broken pattern can expose a false claim, but fear or drunkenness can mislead you.
judge: Compare players whose claims you can check against other information.
Your answer reveals whether their alignments match, not what either role is.
mortician: Wait for a dead player who attracted several visitors if you want the extra name clue.
You can use this ability only once and only while alive.
vigilante: Use other players’ information before declaring a kill; a wrong target can hurt your team.
A Haunt can be a useful target, especially one whose ability triggers on execution.
sheriff: Speak privately with the two named players before revealing the Haunt you were shown.
Check their claims against other evidence; your first-night information may be unreliable.
Completing the Night Rite can refresh your starting clue.
hoflibrarian: Speak privately with the two named players before revealing the Villager you were shown.
Check their claims against other evidence; your first-night information may be unreliable.
Completing the Night Rite can refresh your starting clue.
teacher: Ask your neighbors what they claim before revealing the role you were shown.
Check their claims against other evidence; your first-night information may be unreliable.
Completing the Night Rite can refresh your starting clue.
hunter: If the Horror kills you at night, a Haunt may die too.
A convincing claim to be a valuable information role may draw the Horror’s attack.
drunk: You see guidance for the Villager you believe you are.
hag: Your declaration after death can test a player’s claim to be Good.
Coordinate with allies before choosing a target; a Good player may die.
lostwanderer: Visit an ally who may be targeted. Other visits to them may move to a neighbor.
Coordinate with trusted players so your redirection protects more than it disrupts.
executioner: Your target’s execution wins your personal goal even if you have died.
You may bargain with either team, but reveal your target only when it helps.
researcher: Listen to claims and compare them with other players’ information before naming three roles.
You may declare during the day even after death; all three guesses must be right.
guardian: Learn what your ward needs to survive; they may belong to any team.
Your goal is for your ward to live to the end, even if you die first.
banshee: You want to be executed. Death from a night attack or a Villager ability will not trigger your fear.
Make a plausible claim that invites suspicion without making yourself an obvious kill target.
basilisk: Coordinate with the Horror to fear players whose abilities could expose or protect against them.
Keeping an information role feared can be more useful than eliminating them immediately.
sphinx: Share useful glimpses with your evil team quickly, especially likely information and protection roles.
Use your clues to help the Horror choose kills and the Basilisk choose fear targets.
monster: Choose a victim and one of their living neighbors to fear if that victim dies.
Coordinate bluffs and target choices with your Haunts; a saved victim causes no fear.
wraith: Choose whether your visit is visible to the Watchman and Mortician.
Coordinate your target and cover story with your Haunts; a hidden visit can conceal your attack.
